questions.topic: Magnification of a virtual image

questions.stem: Translator note TR-01 asks how the magnification of an upright virtual image from a magnifying glass should be described in words.

options.text: The image is larger than the object, upright, and located on the same side of the lens as the object
The image is larger than the object, inverted, and located on the far side of the lens
options.misconception: describes a real inverted image as virtual

options.text: The image is the same size as the object, upright, and located at the focal point
options.misconception: confuses a virtual image with a unit-magnification image

options.text: The image is smaller than the object, upright, and located between the lens and the focal point
options.misconception: believes virtual images are always reduced

questions.explanation: A magnifying glass held closer than its focal length gives an upright, enlarged, virtual image on the object's side. The magnification is the ratio of image distance to object distance, and it exceeds one here.

options.text: A real, upright and reduced image forms at the focus on the object's side
options.misconception: places a real image on the wrong side

questions.explanation: A diverging lens always forms a virtual, upright and reduced image between the lens and its near focus on the object's side. No real rays converge, so nothing can be caught on a screen behind the lens.

questions.explanation: A diverging lens spreads the rays from a distant object and their backward extensions meet on the object's side, giving a small upright virtual image. That reduced size widens the field of view.
questions.hint: The virtual image of a diverging lens is small.
